title: Luke Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 18.

questions.question: In Luke 18, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A judge who feared not God
A Pharisee praying in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: A judge who feared not God
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with a parable about a judge who feared not God and regarded not man in Luke 18:2.

questions.question: What did the widow in the city ask the judge to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Avenge her of her adversary
questions.explanation: In Luke 18:3, the widow came to the judge saying, 'Avenge me of mine adversary.'

questions.question: How did the unjust judge initially respond to the widow's requests?
options: He would not respond for a while
questions.correctAnswer: He would not respond for a while
questions.explanation: Luke 18:4 says that the judge would not for a while but afterward said within himself he would avenge her.

questions.question: According to the parable, why did the judge decide to grant the widow justice?
questions.correctAnswer: Because she troubled him continually
questions.explanation: Luke 18:5 states the judge decided to avenge the widow lest her continual coming weary him.

questions.question: What question did Jesus ask about the Son of Man when He comes?
options: Shall he find faith on the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Shall he find faith on the earth?
questions.explanation: Luke 18:8 asks, 'Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?'

questions.question: Who were the two men that went up into the temple to pray?
questions.correctAnswer: A Pharisee and a publican
questions.explanation: Luke 18:10 states that two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.

questions.question: What did the Pharisee thank God for in his prayer?
options: That he was not as other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or as the publican
questions.correctAnswer: That he was not as other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or as the publican
questions.explanation: Luke 18:11 shows the Pharisee thanking God that he was not as other men including the publican.

questions.question: How often did the Pharisee fast according to his prayer?
questions.correctAnswer: Twice in the week
questions.explanation: Luke 18:12 states the Pharisee said, 'I fast twice in the week.'

questions.question: What did the publican do when he prayed in the temple?
options: He would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven but smote upon his breast
questions.correctAnswer: He would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven but smote upon his breast
questions.explanation: Luke 18:13 describes the publican standing afar off, not lifting his eyes but smiting upon his breast.

questions.question: According to Jesus, who was justified rather than the other after praying?
questions.correctAnswer: The publican
questions.explanation: Luke 18:14 says that the publican went down to his house justified rather than the Pharisee.

questions.question: What were the disciples' reactions when infants were brought to Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: They rebuked them
questions.explanation: Luke 18:15 states that when disciples saw infants being brought to Jesus, they rebuked them.

questions.question: Jesus spoke a parable to teach that men ought always to pray and not to faint.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 18:1 says Jesus spoke a parable to the end that men ought always to pray and not to faint.

questions.question: The unjust judge in the parable feared God and regarded man.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 18:2 states the judge feared not God, neither regarded man.

questions.question: The Pharisee boasted about giving tithes of all that he possessed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 18:12 includes the Pharisee saying, 'I give tithes of all that I possess.'

questions.question: Jesus told the parable about a widow who was a queen.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 18:3 refers to the widow in the city, not a queen.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Luke 18:16, why should little children be allowed to come to Him?
options: For of such is the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: For of such is the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: Jesus said, 'Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God' in Luke 18:16.

questions.question: What does Luke 18:30 promise will happen if someone leaves family for the kingdom of God's sake as commanded in verse 29?
options: They shall receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting
They shall be sorrowful but rewarded later
They shall become leaders in the church
They will be tested with many trials
questions.correctAnswer: They shall receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting
questions.explanation: Luke 18:30 states that those who leave house, parents, or family for the kingdom's sake in verse 29 will receive manifold more now and eternal life.

questions.question: What did Jesus say is necessary to enter the kingdom of God according to Luke 18:17?
options: Receive the kingdom of God as a little child
Be a teacher of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Receive the kingdom of God as a little child
questions.explanation: Luke 18:17 says, 'Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.'

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the ruler calling Him 'Good Master' in Luke 18:19 after the ruler asked about inheriting eternal life in verse 18?
options: He questioned why he called Him good, stating only God is good
He affirmed that He was good and could give eternal life
He ignored the compliment and gave a parable
He told him to follow the commandments instead
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why he called Him good, stating only God is good
questions.explanation: In Luke 18:19, Jesus asked, 'Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is, God,' responding directly to the ruler's question in verse 18.

questions.question: Which commandments did Jesus list to the ruler in Luke 18:20?
options: Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother
Love thy neighbor as thyself, Do not steal, Keep the Sabbath holy
Do not kill, Do not covet, Honour the Sabbath
Forgive others, Love God, Do not lie
questions.correctAnswer: Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother
questions.explanation: Luke 18:20 lists these commandments as Jesus' response to the ruler's question about inheriting eternal life.

questions.question: What was the ruler's response to Jesus' commandments in Luke 18:21?
options: All these have I kept from my youth up
I have failed in some but will try harder
I do not understand these commandments
I have not kept them fully
questions.correctAnswer: All these have I kept from my youth up
questions.explanation: The ruler claimed in Luke 18:21 that he had kept all the commandments from his youth.

questions.question: What was the 'one thing' Jesus said the ruler lacked in Luke 18:22?
options: Sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and come, follow me
questions.correctAnswer: Sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and come, follow me
questions.explanation: In Luke 18:22, Jesus told the ruler to sell all he had, give to the poor, and follow Him, indicating what he lacked.

questions.question: How did the ruler react when Jesus told him to sell all and follow Him, according to Luke 18:23?
options: He was very sorrowful because he was very rich
He immediately agreed and followed Jesus
He questioned Jesus about the command
He ignored the command and walked away
questions.correctAnswer: He was very sorrowful because he was very rich
questions.explanation: Luke 18:23 states that the ruler was very sorrowful upon hearing Jesus' command because of his wealth.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the difficulty for rich people to enter the kingdom of God in Luke 18:24-25?
options: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter
Rich people have an advantage entering the kingdom
Rich people must give all to the poor to enter
Rich people cannot enter the kingdom at all
questions.correctAnswer: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter
questions.explanation: Jesus used this metaphor in Luke 18:25 to describe how difficult it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God.

questions.question: How did Jesus address the question 'Who then can be saved?' in Luke 18:27?
options: The things which are impossible with men are possible with God
No one can be saved if rich
Only those who follow the law perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: The things which are impossible with men are possible with God
questions.explanation: Jesus responded in Luke 18:27 that what is impossible for people is possible for God, implying salvation is by God's power.

questions.question: What did Peter claim in Luke 18:28 about following Jesus?
options: We have left all, and followed thee
We have doubts but continue to follow
We have given up some but not all possessions
We are still deciding whether to follow
questions.correctAnswer: We have left all, and followed thee
questions.explanation: Peter said in Luke 18:28 that they had left everything to follow Jesus.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about those who leave family for the kingdom in Luke 18:29-30?
options: They shall receive manifold more now and eternal life in the world to come
They will be rewarded only in heaven
They will be tested severely on earth
They must return to their families later
questions.correctAnswer: They shall receive manifold more now and eternal life in the world to come
questions.explanation: Jesus promised in Luke 18:29-30 that those who sacrifice for the kingdom will receive many blessings now and eternal life later.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus welcomed infants and rebuked His disciples when they tried to prevent the children from coming to Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Luke 18:15-16, Jesus called children to Him and rebuked His disciples for forbidding them.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the rich ruler that keeping the commandments was sufficient to inherit eternal life.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jesus told the ruler in Luke 18:22 that he lacked one thing: to sell all he had and follow Him, showing commandments alone were not enough.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 18:27, salvation depends on human effort and cannot be achieved by God's power alone.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 18:27 states that things impossible for men are possible with God, emphasizing salvation depends on God's power, not human effort.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 18.

questions.question: In Luke 18:31, what does Jesus say will be accomplished when they go up to Jerusalem?
options: All things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished
The kingdom of God shall be established
questions.correctAnswer: All things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished
questions.explanation: Luke 18:31 explicitly states Jesus said, 'all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished.'

questions.question: According to Luke 18:32, which of the following is NOT mentioned as something that will happen to Jesus?
options: He shall be delivered unto the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be crowned king
questions.explanation: Luke 18:32 lists delivery to Gentiles, mocking, spiteful treatment, and spitting on Jesus, but does not mention crowning him king.

questions.question: What event does Jesus predict in Luke 18:33 that will occur on the third day?
options: He shall be resurrected by angels
He shall appear to the Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: He shall rise again
questions.explanation: Luke 18:33 clearly states that on the third day, Jesus shall rise again after being put to death.

questions.question: In Luke 18:34, why did the disciples not understand Jesus' prophecy about his suffering and resurrection?
options: Because the saying was hid from them
Because they were distracted by the crowd
questions.correctAnswer: Because the saying was hid from them
questions.explanation: Luke 18:34 says, 'this saying was hid from them,' indicating divine concealment of the meaning of Jesus' prophecy.

questions.question: In Luke 18:38, how does the blind man address Jesus?
options: Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me
questions.explanation: Luke 18:38 records the blind man crying out, 'Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.'

questions.question: What does Jesus say to the blind man in Luke 18:42 that indicates the man's faith was crucial for his healing?
options: Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee
Go in peace, your faith is strong
Because of your belief, you are made whole
questions.correctAnswer: Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee
questions.explanation: Luke 18:42 explicitly states, 'thy faith hath saved thee,' emphasizing faith's role in the healing.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐμπαίζω' (empaizō) in Luke 18:32 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To mock or ridicule
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ἐμπαίζω' in Luke 18:32 means 'to mock or ridicule,' describing how Jesus will be treated.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Luke 18:31-33 where Jesus predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection?
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic foreshadowing
questions.explanation: Luke 18:31-33 uses prophetic foreshadowing to predict Jesus’ passion and resurrection, a common literary device in prophetic texts.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is connected to Jesus' prediction of being 'delivered unto the Gentiles' and mocked in Luke 18:32?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 22:7-8
questions.explanation: Psalm 22:7-8 describes the mocking and scorn Jesus predicts in Luke 18:32, linking His passion to this Messianic psalm.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of faith being necessary for healing as seen in Luke 18:42?
questions.correctAnswer: Mark 10:52
questions.explanation: Mark 10:52 recounts the healing of blind Bartimaeus where Jesus says, 'thy faith hath made thee whole,' paralleling Luke 18:42.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus’ statement about going to Jerusalem in Luke 18:31?
options: Peter's declaration that they have left all to follow Jesus
The parable of the persistent widow
The healing of the blind man near Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: Peter's declaration that they have left all to follow Jesus
questions.explanation: Luke 18:28-30 records Peter’s statement about leaving all for Jesus, which immediately precedes Luke 18:31.

questions.question: What type of literary structure can be identified in Luke 18:9-14 regarding the Pharisee and the publican?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Luke 18:9-14 uses parallelism contrasting two prayers to highlight humility versus self-righteousness.

questions.question: How does the healing of the blind man in Luke 18:35-43 typologically foreshadow Jesus' resurrection mentioned in Luke 18:33?
options: The restoration of sight symbolizes new spiritual life after resurrection
The blind man’s following Jesus is a metaphor for resurrection
The miracle was performed on the third day
The blind man was a prophet predicting resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: The restoration of sight symbolizes new spiritual life after resurrection
questions.explanation: The healing restores physical and spiritual sight, typologically linking to resurrection as new life in Luke 18:33.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy is fulfilled by Jesus' entry near Jericho and the healing of the blind man as described in Luke 18:35-43?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 35:5-6
questions.explanation: Isaiah 35:5-6 prophesies the opening of blind eyes and healing, fulfilled in Jesus’ healing in Luke 18:35-43.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 18:34, the disciples fully understood Jesus' predictions about his death and resurrection at the time he spoke them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 18:34 states the disciples 'understood none of these things' and the saying was hid from them, indicating lack of understanding.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 18:1 teach about the nature of prayer and perseverance in faith?
options: Prayer must be continual and persistent without losing heart
Prayer is effective only when it is brief and infrequent
God answers only once and does not require repeated requests
Faith is irrelevant to prayer's effectiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer must be continual and persistent without losing heart
questions.explanation: Luke 18:1 teaches that men ought always to pray and not to faint, emphasizing perseverance in prayer as essential to faith

questions.question: What doctrine about God's justice is taught in Luke 18:7?
options: God will swiftly avenge and vindicate His elect who cry to Him
God is indifferent to the prayers of His elect
God delays justice because He cannot act quickly
God's elect must earn their vindication through works
questions.correctAnswer: God will swiftly avenge and vindicate His elect who cry to Him
questions.explanation: Luke 18:7 affirms that God will avenge His elect who cry day and night to Him, highlighting divine justice in response to persistent prayer

questions.question: What doctrine about justification and humility does Luke 18:14 teach?
options: Those who humble themselves will be exalted and justified before God
Self-exaltation is the path to justification
Justification depends on public recognition of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Those who humble themselves will be exalted and justified before God
questions.explanation: Luke 18:14 states that everyone who exalts himself will be abased, and he who humbles himself will be exalted, teaching justification is linked to humility

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 18:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Luke 18:5 shows the judge’s reluctance to avenge immediately but eventually yielding, illustrating the attribute of longsuffering as God patiently responds to persistent prayer

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated in Luke 18:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Luke 18:27 teaches that what is impossible with men is possible with God, demonstrating God's omnipotence

questions.question: How does Luke 18:31–33 connect to the broader redemptive-historical theme of Christ's passion?
options: It explicitly predicts Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection as fulfillment of prophecy
It describes Christ’s triumphant earthly reign
It emphasizes Christ’s avoidance of suffering
It focuses on the establishment of the Mosaic Law
questions.correctAnswer: It explicitly predicts Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection as fulfillment of prophecy
questions.explanation: Luke 18:31–33 records Jesus foretelling his passion and resurrection, linking to Old Testament prophecy and the central redemptive event

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Luke 18:16–17 establish about children and the kingdom of God?
options: Receiving the kingdom of God requires childlike humility and trust
Children are excluded from the kingdom of God
The kingdom is only for the learned and powerful
Salvation is earned through ascetic works
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving the kingdom of God requires childlike humility and trust
questions.explanation: Luke 18:16–17 emphasizes that one must receive the kingdom as a little child, highlighting humility and dependence as prerequisites

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 18:22 and 18:25 teach about riches and salvation?
options: Riches can hinder entrance into the kingdom of God due to reliance on worldly wealth
Riches guarantee entrance to the kingdom
Salvation is independent of attitude toward wealth
Poverty is a sin that prevents salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Riches can hinder entrance into the kingdom of God due to reliance on worldly wealth
questions.explanation: Luke 18:22 commands selling all and giving to the poor, and 18:25 states it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter the kingdom, teaching the obstacle riches pose

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 18:13 and 18:14 teach about repentance and justification?
options: True justification comes from humble repentance, not self-righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: True justification comes from humble repentance, not self-righteousness
questions.explanation: Luke 18:13 shows the publican’s humble plea for mercy, and 18:14 declares the humble will be exalted, teaching repentance precedes justification

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 18:29 and 18:30 teach about discipleship and reward?
options: Sacrificial discipleship for the kingdom results in manifold blessings now and eternal life
There is no reward for forsaking family for Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrificial discipleship for the kingdom results in manifold blessings now and eternal life
questions.explanation: Luke 18:29–30 promises that those who leave family for the kingdom’s sake will receive manifold blessings in this life and eternal life, teaching reward for faithful discipleship

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jesus’ command to the rich ruler to sell all (Luke 18:22–23) is an impossible requirement for salvation. What does Luke 18:22–27 actually teach?
options: Salvation is possible with God’s power despite human inability to fully meet this demand
Salvation requires perfect adherence to selling all possessions
Only the rich are excluded from salvation
Jesus teaches salvation is earned by wealth redistribution
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is possible with God’s power despite human inability to fully meet this demand
questions.explanation: Luke 18:27 clarifies that what is impossible for men is possible with God, showing divine grace enables salvation despite human weakness

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 18:43 teach about faith and healing?
options: Faith is instrumental in receiving both physical healing and salvation
Faith is irrelevant to physical restoration
Healing is purely miraculous without human response
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is instrumental in receiving both physical healing and salvation
questions.explanation: Luke 18:42 states the blind man’s faith saved him, and 18:43 shows he immediately received sight, linking faith to healing

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly illustrated by Jesus’ response to the blind man in Luke 18:40–42?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Jesus’ compassionate command to heal the blind man (Luke 18:40–42) demonstrates God’s attribute of mercy

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 18:9 and 18:11 teach about human self-righteousness and the reality of sin?
options: Self-righteousness blinds people to their own sinfulness, whereas true repentance acknowledges sin
Self-righteousness is the path to justification
Sin is minimized in the eyes of the Pharisee
All men are equally righteous before God
questions.correctAnswer: Self-righteousness blinds people to their own sinfulness, whereas true repentance acknowledges sin
questions.explanation: Luke 18:9 shows some trusted in themselves as righteous, while 18:11 reveals the Pharisee’s pride, contrasting with acknowledgment of sin needed for salvation

questions.question: How does Luke 18:34 illustrate the cognitive condition of the disciples regarding Jesus’ prediction of His passion?
options: The disciples did not understand or grasp the necessity of Jesus’ suffering and resurrection
The disciples fully comprehended Jesus’ mission
The disciples rejected Jesus’ words as false
The disciples immediately spread the message of resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: The disciples did not understand or grasp the necessity of Jesus’ suffering and resurrection
questions.explanation: Luke 18:34 states that the saying was hidden from the disciples and they did not understand, indicating spiritual blindness to the passion narrative
